tools.name: task
tools.description:
Delegate a job to one subagent. The subagent runs in its own fresh context, receives only
your prompt, and returns a final text or finished piece.

- Make the prompt self-contained: include the material / doc slices it needs.
- Say exactly what it must return.
- Keep it to one coherent job. A prompt packing several unrelated questions makes the subagent burn
  its step budget switching topics; split those into separate delegations.

Delegate when the work would flood you with material you will not reference again — reading around,
trial and error, dead ends — and you need back only the conclusion. Do it yourself when it is a step
or two, or when the work needs going back and forth with the user. A chapter's prose is yours either
way: you write it yourself, never through a subagent. Every delegation asks the user first, and the
subagent sees nothing but the prompt you write for it. The delegable agents and when to use each are
listed below.
- After a planner returns, your next tool call must be propose-plan. Do not start creating the plan's
  cards, world pages, or prose before the user approves it, and do not spend the turn asking about its
  open questions first — put the plan in front of the user and let them rule on it.

可委派的 subagent：
- planner: The chapter planner. Turns one chapter's intent into an executable plan: the beats in order, the characters it must land, the facts that had to be checked with their sources, and the artifacts the chapter lands in.
Use this when the user asks for a chapter's prose and no plan for that chapter exists yet — it reads the design docs end to end and returns one plan you then put in front of the user via propose-plan.
Not for prose — you write that yourself. Not for a fact one lookup settles, or for a design call: use webfetch, the researcher, or the user.
- researcher: The fact-checker. Researches the real world and returns findings with their sources — how a period's office or tax really worked, what a thing was called, how far a weapon reached.
Use this when the novel needs a fact you must not assert from memory and settling it will take several searches and reads: it returns the conclusion and its sources, not the pages it read to get there. For a fact one lookup settles, call webfetch yourself instead. It reads the project but never writes the book — you decide what lands. Findings it expects to be asked again it keeps in its own research notes, so a later session does not look them up twice.

agent.description: Subagent id (see the delegable list below)

prompt.description: Complete task description for the subagent; include all needed material/slices

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read one document, or a single section of it, by its project-relative path.

path: a path incl. its root and extension — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md,
design/wiki/地理.md, design/characters/沈越.md, design/outline/vol_2.md, design/outline/vol_2/s1.md,
chapters/chapter_ch2_v1.md, state/characters/沈越.md, state/progress.md. This is the same path form
every other tool takes.
section (optional): an exact heading title inside that doc, e.g. 一句话简介, 题材 · 频道, 角色：沈越,
本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

path.description: Document path incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/characters/林晚.md, chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md

section.description: Optional: exact section heading to read only that section

tools.name: write
tools.description:
Write a complete file in one shot: create it, or replace it entirely.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- The content IS the file — it is written byte for byte. So it holds document text and nothing
  else: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions. Undecided fields become （待定）.
- Use this when you are the author of the whole file. To change part of a file that already
  exists, use `edit` instead: it needs only the piece you are changing, and the user reviews a
  diff of that piece rather than re-reading the whole document.
- Writing asks the user first: they are shown a diff of what will land, and can accept or refuse.
  If they refuse, nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Re-running it on a file you have not re-read may overwrite someone else's change; the write is
  refused if the file moved on since you read it, in which case read it again.

path.description: Project-relative path: design/<...> (design docs) or chapters/<...> (finished prose)

content.description: The complete file content, byte for byte

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Replace exact text inside one file that already exists.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- `find` is the text to replace, copied from what you read. Give it enough surrounding context to
  be unique. Keep the indentation exactly as it appears — and never include line-number prefixes.
- `replace` is what goes in its place, and must differ from `find`.
- If `find` matches more than one place the edit is refused: add surrounding lines to make it
  unique, or set `all` to change every occurrence (a rename, say).
- If `find` is not found, read the file again and copy the text from there. These differences are
  tolerated without complaint — per-line leading/trailing whitespace, indentation, line endings,
  and curly versus straight quotes; the match is fuzzy and it tells you when it had to be.
- Refused outright if the fuzzy match would swallow far more than `find` describes — that means
  the anchor was too loose; give a longer, more precise `find`.
- `find` must not be empty. To create a file or replace one entirely, use `write` instead.
- Editing asks the user first: they see a diff of just this change, and can accept or refuse. If
  they refuse nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Refused if the file moved on since you read it; read it again and redo the edit on the current text.

path.description: Project-relative path to an existing file: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

find.description: The exact text to replace, with enough context to be unique

replace.description: The text to put in its place; must differ from find

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

tools.name: delete
tools.description:
Delete a whole file — a design doc, a character card, a chapter.

- `path` is project-relative: `design/<...>`, `chapters/<...>` or `state/<...>`.
- **Look at where the name still appears before you delete it.** That reference check is shown to the
  user together with the request. If the term is still mentioned elsewhere, decide whether those
  places should be cleaned up too — and clean them yourself with `edit`, one place at a time. The
  tool does not cascade: which references matter is a judgement about the story, not a rule.
  Leaving a dangling reference is worse than the deletion itself.
- `term` is what to look references up by. It defaults to the filename without its extension
  (`characters/林晚.md` → `林晚`), which is right for cards and topic pages; pass it explicitly when
  the filename is not the name the prose uses.
- To remove only *part* of a file — a paragraph, one section — use `edit` instead: give the exact
  text and an empty replacement. This tool is for the whole file.
- Deleting asks the user first, and they see exactly what will be removed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the file to delete: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

term.description: Name to look up references by before deleting; defaults to the filename without its extension

tools.name: propose-design
tools.description:
Present a whole draft of a design doc for the user to review. Nothing is saved and the turn ends, so
they can approve, refuse, or ask for changes.

Name the target with `path`: its project-relative path incl. root and extension —
design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md,
design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md (volume and sequence outlines),
design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no
character-specific tool for that). Same path form every other tool takes.

**This is for whole documents only.** To change part of an existing doc — a sentence, one section —
use `edit`: the user reviews a diff of just that piece instead of re-reading the whole document, and
it costs you far fewer tokens. A draft is refused only when its kind has a fixed shape (see
design-spec — it holds the shape of every document kind) and the draft does not fill it, since
the user would then be shown blanks while the prose landed anyway. Kinds that are free-form (sequence
outlines, character cards, topic pages) are shown whole, as a single block. Fields you
cannot fill yet get （待定）.

**The draft IS the file**: on approval it is written byte for byte. So the content holds document
text and nothing else — no notes to the user ("暂用名，待你定"), no rationale ("这句是配的试镜台词，
你可以换掉"), no questions ("他要的是真相还是道歉？"). Undecided things become （待定） and nothing
more. Say all of that in your message BEFORE calling this, not inside the draft. Once the user
answers, apply-design lands it.

If the user asks for changes, revise the whole draft and call this again — it replaces the previous
proposal, which is what you want: only the version they last saw can be landed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the document, incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md, design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no character-specific tool)

content.description: The complete document. It IS the file: on approval it is written byte for byte, so it may contain document text only — no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions; undecided fields become （待定）

tools.name: apply-design
tools.description:
Write a reviewed proposal to disk. Takes only the target — the text is the version the user just read,
so there is nothing to pass. Identify it exactly as you proposed it: `path`, the same project-relative
path.

Call it once the user approves the proposal you presented. It is refused when no proposal is
pending, when the user has not agreed (their reply must be an approval, not a request for changes),
or when the document changed since you proposed it. In all those cases: propose-design again with
the updated text.

Never use it to write text the user has not seen.

path.description: The same project-relative path you proposed it with

tools.name: propose-plan
tools.description:
Present one chapter's plan for the user's approval, and end the turn. Nothing of the chapter is
written yet — this is the step before writing, and the turn ends here so the user can judge the plan.

Call it once the plan for ONE chapter is ready: yours, or the planner's when the material was not
already in hand. The plan is saved as the chapter's plan artifact, so the user's answer applies to
exactly the bytes they were shown; calling it again for the same chapter replaces that artifact.

Write a scene brief, not a step-by-step script. The prose writer needs room to invent blocking,
dialogue, timing and emphasis; the plan fixes what happens, not where the camera sits.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

## 依据
One line: which sequence function this chapter advances, and what changes (information, relationship,
resource, position, cognition).

## 前情
2–4 sentences. Only what the reader must know entering this scene: who these people are to each other
right now, what each of them wants, and what is already settled. Do not recap the whole book or the
world.

## 这场戏
One continuous scene: where and when, who is present, what each person wants, who blocks the
protagonist, and what is at stake. The protagonist must have a live person to act against, not only
an interior realization — even a quiet chapter needs someone in the room who wants something and
resists.

## 必须发生
3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not write camera
directions, word counts, “放大点”, or “第 1 步 / 第 2 步”.

## 不能提前兑现
What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

## 章末问题
The question the chapter leaves open — an interrupted action, a discovery, a relationship shift, or a
new question. Do not force a cliffhanger.

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/<名>.md for a new character, or design/wiki/<page>.md for a new world fact.
  These are listed first because they still land through propose-design, before the prose; never
  write prose around a missing prerequisite.
- The chapter file: chapters/chapter_ch<N>_v<M>.md.
- Only the state files this chapter actually moves (state/characters/<名>.md, state/foreshadowing.md,
  state/progress.md). state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters, one section per chapter,
  two lines each.

No 题材, no separate 意图, no 价值变化 section, no step-by-step beats, no per-step word budgets, no
“放大点”, no execution red lines. Those were the old execution script; the brief replaces them.

## 依据
本章承担全书的开门功能——“金手指首次露面”：沈越当众看见一行只有他能读到的扉页字迹，且为此付出现实的代价；改变的是信息（这行字真实存在、别人看不见、他能反复读到）和处境（他手上多了一本不在处置清单上的书，且欠下或损失了什么）。

## 前情
沈越是这家武汉老城区旧书店的帮工，日常的活是清点、分拣、把该走的书挑出来抱到门口。店已经撑不住，能腾的现钱和能留的东西都很少，谁的账都拖不起。今天傍晚有人上门按斤收旧书，谈好的价钱已经说出口，那一摞书过秤、装车就走了。沈越只站在处置权的边角上：他决定哪一本先被抱走，不决定任何一本书的去留。

## 这场戏
营业日的傍晚，快到打烊，店里堆着清出来的旧书，门口一辆三轮、一杆秤。在场两人：沈越，和那个每月来一趟、按斤收旧书的人（人名待定）。沈越要的是把这半天清完、数目对得上、不惹事；收书的人要的是趁着天还没黑把秤过完、把车蹬走，话不多说一句。冲突落在一摞已经捆好、正等着上秤的书上：沈越从最上面一本翻到扉页，看见一行字，抬头再看对面那张毫无反应的脸——对方看不见。从这一刻起他要干的事变成让这本书不出这道门，而他说不出一句真话。赌注是这本书、他这半天的工钱、和收书人往后怎么看他这个人。

## 必须发生
- 沈越在书的扉页上看见一行字；他做最省事的一次验证——把同一页递过去，对方看到的就是一页什么都没有的东西，随手又递回来。
- 收书的人开始动手处置这摞书：拎起绳子往秤钩上挂，或者在货单上划掉它、把书往车上码；沈越必须当着对方的面把这本书截下来，动作大得反常。
- 他给不出真话，只能当场现编一个能站住的说法；对方不认，把话堵回来，并且把条件摆到桌面上——要留这本书，就得有人掏钱把它从这一摞里买出来。
- 沈越接下条件并当场兑现：钱从他自己口袋里出去，那笔钱对他不是小数；书留下，这一摞过秤的数目少了，他这半天的活等于白干，收书的人临走撂下一句不好听的评价。
- 三轮车走了，剩下的一摞从店里彻底消失、追不回来；沈越一个人把书合上、再翻开，挪到灯下重看，那行字还在，一个字都没变。

## 不能提前兑现
- 只给“第一行”，不给后面：写信人是谁、要交给谁、这本书为什么在这里，一概不给；也不暗示它与沈越本人或这家店有牵连。
- 金手指的来源、代价、覆盖范围不解释；本章不出现第二本带字迹的书，也不给“别人隐约觉得这页奇怪”之类的旁证。
- “离开老城区字迹会消失”这条规则本章不得被试验、不得被任何角色说出口，沈越连想都想不到去试。
- 书店的经济结局（关不关、欠多少）只作为在场的压力存在，不给人一句话说死，也不报出具体数目。
- 沈越为什么留在这家店（欠人情、无处可去、还是别的）不解释。

## 章末问题
这行字是专门留给他的，还是留给任何一个翻开这本书的人？——而店里剩下的旧书，是不是每一本扉页上都压着一行。

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/沈越.md：本章每个选择都压在他还没定的底牌上（年龄、为何在这家店、经济状况、说话的分寸），缺此不可动笔。
- design/wiki/扉页.md：先把字迹的形态钉死——笔迹与颜色、占扉页什么位置、旁人看到的是什么、能不能拍照或临摹、隔一会儿再翻开会怎样；否则第一章的“第一次”和后文对不上。
- design/wiki/world.md 补“空间与舞台”的落点：老城区哪一片、街名与店名、店面形制与打烊时间。
- design/characters/〈收书人〉.md：一页即可，不进长期阵容；但必须写清他凭什么有权处置这批书、多久来一趟。
- chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md
- state/characters/沈越.md：手上有一本不在处置清单上的书、今天损失了什么、明天还上不上班。
- state/foreshadowing.md：这本书与这行字埋于第 1 章，回收章节未定、未回收。
- state/progress.md：第 1 章，两行。

# 核心设定

男频
都市

一个在旧书店整理旧书的人。

武汉老城区，一家濒临倒闭的旧书店。

1. 按 propose-plan 的既定格式写一份第 1 章的规划：## 依据 / ## 前情 / ## 这场戏 / ## 必须发生 / ## 不能提前兑现 / ## 章末问题 / ## 产物（按序）。写场景简报，不写分镜、不写字数预算、不写“第几步”。

4. 单独列出“材料缺口清单”：现有文档不足以支撑规划、必须由用户回答的问题，最多 3 条，每条附你的推荐。
5. 不要写正文。

两层联排小楼，天井、石库门、红砖青瓦，写满了年代感。这些分布在武汉市各处的中西合璧样式小楼，组成了武汉最具代表性的建筑群落，是老武汉九省通衢的历史见证，被称为“老里份”。

如今，“老里份”正在变身新“网红”。

在建成于1910年的巴公房子前拍照打卡，到始建于1912年的保元里体验一场沉浸式戏剧，去始建于1933年的延庆里选购一件手工艺术品……每逢节假日，很多年轻人涌进汉口历史风貌区观光、游玩。

城市更新过程中，武汉市在文脉赓续上持续用力，让历史文脉成为城市的“金名片”。

本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

List the project's documents with, under each, its section headings — so you know what material

tools.name: webfetch
tools.description:
Fetch one URL and return its content as text / markdown / raw html.

url: must start with http:// or https://
format (optional): text | markdown | html — default markdown (best for reading a web page)
timeout (optional): seconds, default 30, max 120

HTML pages are converted per format; plain files (txt/md/json…) are returned as-is; images/PDF

numResults (optional): how many results; max 10. Defaults to the deployment setting

tools.name: recall
tools.description:
Look in this book's research notes: findings earlier research already settled, each with the date it
was checked and its sources. Read it before you search — a question this book has looked up before
should not be looked up again.

query (optional): words to look for in the notes' titles and bodies, e.g. 佃租, 漕运, 爽点节奏.

still holds. If its scope, era or date does not fit the question you were given, verify on the web
anyway and rewrite that same note. Matching is literal — a query that finds nothing returns the list
of titles, so retry with the note's own wording, or call with no query at all.

query.description: Words to look for in the notes' titles and bodies. Omit to list what is already recorded.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

encyclopedia, no 题材.

3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not prescribe

What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

“老里份”变身新“网红” 文化出新添魅力

两层联排小楼，天井、石库门、红砖青瓦，写满了年代感。这些分布在武汉市各处的中西合璧样式小楼，组成了武汉最具代表性的建筑群落，是老武汉九省通衢的历史见证，被称为“老里份”。

如今，“老里份”正在变身新“网红”。

在建成于1910年的巴公房子前拍照打卡，到始建于1912年的保元里体验一场沉浸式戏剧，去始建于1933年的延庆里选购一件手工艺术品……每逢节假日，很多年轻人涌进汉口历史风貌区观光、游玩。

6. 章末：沈越独自把那一行字再读一遍，发现他刚才读到的字在变/或者后面还有半行没显出来？—— Cautious: 不能提前演示"离开老城区消失"。Maybe 章末: 他抬头看见店里某一处（门口/招牌）与那行字里提到的东西对上，或者他想到要查这个人是谁，但书里再没有第二个字。Keep: 他弄清这一行字指向一个他认得的东西（店里的旧账本/库房编号/一个没寄出的信封里同笔迹），但当他想再找第二行时，扉页又只剩那一行——机制不全揭。

Careful not to invent content that requires user approval. I'll phrase as "指向书店里已有的某样东西（候选：旧账本/进货单/未寄出的信——由用户定）". Maybe too many options create mush. It's acceptable as the brief defers.

不能提前兑现: 
- 不解释机制（为什么只有沈越看见、字迹为何只在老城区、字迹从哪来）; 不做"离开老城区"的实证（本章不让他走出老城区验证消失）。
- 不挑明逝者身份与沈越的关系，不揭示遗言全文（只出第一行/半句）。
- 不让第二个人知道金手指（收旧书的人、店主、任何在场者都只当他是恋书的怪人）。
- 不定书店结局（保下/拆掉/转手）。
- 全书没有卷纲层，因此没有禁揭清单可依 —— 这是我列的临时禁揭：具体待用户/卷纲确认。
- 也不能提前让"按斤卖书"变成废纸的行业悲剧论述/内心独白化的煽情 — hmm that's execution. Skip.

章末问题: 这一行字要沈越做什么/这本书为什么在他手上——他能不能在下一趟称书的人来之前弄明白，且不让任何人知道他在乎这本书。

产物（按序）with why:
1. design/characters/沈越.md —— 前置：主角卡空着，写手不知道他为什么站在这堆书里、他缺什么、他不敢承认什么；本章的每个取舍都得从他的处境里长出来。
2. design/wiki/旧书店.md（或 world.md 新增页：书店与账）—— 前置：店名、位置（哪条街/哪片里份）、开了多少年、库房多大、欠多少租、期限几天，全是地名与数字，用户定；这些直接决定"按斤算能抵多少租"这场争执的分量。
3. design/wiki/金手指规则.md（或 world.md 的 规则与秩序 扩写）—— 前置：字迹出现的条件（哪些书、何时出现、看得出多少）、"老城区"的边界怎么划、别人看见的是空白还是像褪色墨迹；本章的"试探"一招就靠这条规则，写手不能自己填空。
4. design/characters/<在场者名>.md —— 前置：需要用户给名；没有卡，写手会给这个按斤收书的人临时编性格、行话、价码，日后要返工。
   (note: 也可考虑常客/店主卡)
5. chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md —— 本章正文。
6. state/characters/沈越.md —— 本章后他的处境变化（欠了多少钱/还欠租、手里多了什么书、谁起了疑）。
7. state/foreshadowing.md —— 那行字、那本书、称书人下次上门的期限，三条要挂上账。
8. state/progress.md —— 只有一个 chapter，写一段两行。

Also note "state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters".

Now, should I do more research? The 废纸/旧书回收价 by 斤 — plausible: 旧书按斤收 1–2 元/斤? I shouldn't assert a number. I'll say 价码由用户/资料定 or "按斤开价" without number, and mark that the 斤价 is a real-world number I did not verify — actually I could quickly search. It would add grounding to the stakes. Let me do one quick search on 武汉 废纸 回收价 一斤 2025 and 旧书 按斤 收购价. It's cheap. Also 门面租金 in 昙华林 — could be a big number; better leave to user or verify. Let me search both quickly in one block.

Read one document, or a single section of it, by its project-relative path.

path: a path incl. its root and extension — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md,
design/wiki/地理.md, design/characters/沈越.md, design/outline/vol_2.md, design/outline/vol_2/s1.md,
chapters/chapter_ch2_v1.md, state/characters/沈越.md, state/progress.md. This is the same path form
every other tool takes.
section (optional): an exact heading title inside that doc, e.g. 一句话简介, 题材 · 频道, 角色：沈越,
本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

path.description: Document path incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/characters/林晚.md, chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md

section.description: Optional: exact section heading to read only that section

tools.name: list
tools.description:
List the project's documents with, under each, its section headings — so you know what material
exists, how to address sections, and which items are still placeholder （待定）. Call this before
editing.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the listing — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it for the whole project.

Character cards are one line each: `名字 · 身份（必有齐／待补：…；另有：…）`. “待补”lists
required sections that are still empty; “另有”lists the card's free-form sections beyond the
five required ones, so you can see what is on a card without reading it. Read the card itself
with read to get its content.

Docs that carry no sections (sequence outlines, `design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md`) also get one line:
the path plus the first sentence of the prose, so you can tell which sequence is which without
reading it. Volume outlines (`design/outline/vol_<N>.md`) do list their six sections.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the listing: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Search a word (character / setting / term) across the project and return file + section + line hits.
Hits are reported with project-relative paths (design/characters/沈越.md), the same form every other
tool takes.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the search — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it to search everything, which is what you want before renaming or
removing a name: the prose under chapters/ mentions characters and settings too, and those references
must be cleaned up as well.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the search: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: webfetch
tools.description:
Fetch one URL and return its content as text / markdown / raw html.

url: must start with http:// or https://
format (optional): text | markdown | html — default markdown (best for reading a web page)
timeout (optional): seconds, default 30, max 120

HTML pages are converted per format; plain files (txt/md/json…) are returned as-is; images/PDF
are rejected. Large pages are truncated with a note. Use when the story needs a fact, setting,
or reference material you should not rely on from memory — then reason from what came back.
When DeepSeek Fetch is configured, text/markdown come from its Fetch API (Markdown); html still
uses a direct fetch.

tools.name: websearch
tools.description:
Search the web and return a numbered list of results (title / url / snippet).

query: the search query
numResults (optional): how many results; max 10. Defaults to the deployment setting
(10 with DeepSeek, otherwise 6).

Use to find sources on a topic, then webfetch the promising URLs for full content. Backend:
DeepSeek Search when configured, otherwise tavily when a TAVILY_API_KEY is set, else bocha/exa,
else duckduckgo (no key, best effort). When DeepSeek is not configured, explicitly switch with
TALEMATE_WEBSEARCH_PROVIDER=tavily|bocha|exa|duckduckgo.

numResults.description: Number of results; default 10 when DeepSeek is configured (settings), otherwise 6; max 10

tools.name: recall
tools.description:
Look in this book's research notes: findings earlier research already settled, each with the date it
was checked and its sources. Read it before you search — a question this book has looked up before
should not be looked up again.

query (optional): words to look for in the notes' titles and bodies, e.g. 佃租, 漕运, 爽点节奏.
Omit it to list what is already recorded.

A hit is a lead, not an answer: every note carries its date and sources so you can judge whether it
still holds. If its scope, era or date does not fit the question you were given, verify on the web
anyway and rewrite that same note. Matching is literal — a query that finds nothing returns the list
of titles, so retry with the note's own wording, or call with no query at all.

query.description: Words to look for in the notes' titles and bodies. Omit to list what is already recorded.

response.text:
## 依据

本项目只有 `design/core.md` 和 `design/wiki/world.md` 两页：**没有卷纲、没有序号大纲、没有角色卡、没有已写章节**，所以本章没有“序列约定”可依（sequence contract 缺失这件事本身是缺口，见末）。本章推进的是把设定变成经验：让“他能看见旧书扉页上的字迹”从一条规则变成一件发生在他身上、并且**付了代价**的事；同时用一批随时会被按斤称走的书，把“这家店快要没了”从背景变成本章内的时钟。变化的是：信息（他确认别人看不见那行字）、资源（他为一本书付了代价）、关系（他对一个活人第一次隐瞒）、处境（下一次称书的日期被钉死）。

## 前情

沈越是这家旧书店里整理旧书的人。店里已经定了：库房那批书不再按本卖，而是当旧纸按斤处理，期限很近。他今天的活是把库房分拣完——能单卖的挑出来，剩下的等着过秤。他自己也说不清为什么总要在这堆书里多待一会儿，只知道手上这一箱他想再翻一遍。

## 这场戏

**地点时间**：武汉老城区一家旧书店，店堂连着后间库房；一个没什么客人的下午，雨刚停，街上人少，屋里灯管有一支是坏的。
**在场**：沈越；按斤收旧书废纸的人上门来拉货。店主（或让店关门的那个人）不在场，只以期限和一句交代压着。
**各人要什么**：沈越要把手上这一箱分拣完，至少留下他自己挑出来的那几本；收书的人要今天就把能装的装走、按斤结钱、赶下一家的活，而且他不听“这本不能按斤”这种话。
**谁挡他**：收书的人。他只看斤两、品相和车上还剩多少空位，理由都成立，还带着一身雨气和一辆停在门口的三轮。
**赌注**：这批书一上车就再也回不来；沈越既没有立场也没有钱拦，他身上那点钱买不了几斤；而他在争的这一箱里有一本，扉页上有一行别人看不见的字。

**在场者候选（需用户拍板，不由我定名）**

- **A 收旧书的人在场＋店主以期限缺席压迫**（推荐）：冲突是一个真人、一堆真斤两、一辆真车，不需要先交代沈越的家事。代价：这是一次性配角，必须预留他再来的理由（固定上门日／他其实认得这行的书／他跟店主是老关系），否则下一章没有压力；店主缺席也让第一章少一个能追问的人。
- **B 店主本人全程在场，一边清库房一边跟沈越算账**：张力最直接，也是唯一能问“你留着这本干什么”的人。代价：他精明就会追问那本书，金手指的保密成本立刻抬高；而且他跟沈越是什么关系（雇主／亲戚／受托人）必须先由用户定，否则他要退化成讲解背景的嘴。
- **C 家里人上门来催他别再耗着**：压力最靠近“离开老城区字迹就消失”这条规则，人物立场天生对立。代价：第一章就摆家事会把书与遗言的戏份挤薄，而且要先补出家庭结构（谁、为什么催、催他去哪）。

## 必须发生

- 收书的人上门，先看货再开价，把库房那批整体按斤判了；沈越拦下其中一箱，理由是能对活人说出口的（缺册、水渍、有批注、品相还行），对方逐条驳，驳得有理。
- 沈越为一个具体的东西付出代价：掏自己的钱买下、答应替对方跑一趟活、或把好的几本单独挑给他在价钱上让一步——代价落在他身上，钱、时间或脸面，一样不能白让。
- 他在争到手里的那本书上翻扉页，看见多出一行字；他做一次试探：把书递过去或侧过去，问一句“这上头有字吧”。对方只看见空白，或只当是褪了色的旧印，随口把话岔开——第一层确认落地。
- 他必须当场决定这本书的去向，并对外给出一个过得去的解释（残本、缺页、留着自己看），第一次对活人隐瞒。
- 收书的人装车走人，把话留下：下一趟哪天来、要装多少、按什么算——外部时钟钉死，并且沈越当场就知道自己下次同样拦不住。
- 门关上后他再看那一行字：字还在，只这一行，翻遍前后再没有第二行；而这一行指向店里已经有的某样东西（旧账本／进货单／一叠没寄出的信——由用户定，此处不替他选）。

## 不能提前兑现

- 不解释字迹从哪来、为什么只有他能看见；本章**不让他走出老城区去验证“离开就消失”**，这条规则第一章只作为他自己心里知道的事存在，不上演、不实验。
- 不揭逝者身份，不揭遗言全文，只出这一行；这一行不能一次说清是谁写给谁、欠的是什么。
- 不让第二个人知道金手指：在场的人只当他是个舍不得书的怪人，或者一个揽事的临时工。
- 不定书店结局：保下来、拆掉、转手，一个答案都不给。
- **禁揭项**：本项目没有卷纲层，因此不存在正式的 禁揭 清单。以上四条是按 core／world 推出来的临时禁揭；卷纲补齐后必须复核，尤其“字迹只在老城区”这条规则的显形时机。

## 章末问题

这一行字要他去做什么？以及：在下一次称书的车来之前，他能不能弄明白，又不让任何人看出他为什么非留这本书不可。

## 产物（按序）

- `design/characters/沈越.md`（新角色卡，前置）——主角卡是空的，写手不知道他为什么留在这家店里、缺什么、怕什么；本章他每一次让步和耍横都得从他的处境里长出来，卡不补只能靠猜。
- `design/wiki/旧书店.md`（新世界事实页，前置）——店名、所在街区（哪片里份、哪条街，地名必须用户给）、开了多少年、库房多大、欠多少租、期限还剩几天。这些数字直接决定“按斤能抵多少租”这场争执的分量。可用的现实量级（已核，但只是量级不是设定）：老城区小门面月租约 2000–4500 元（2025–2026 挂牌），旧书废纸按斤 0.6–1.1 元／斤（回收站与智能回收价）。
- `design/wiki/金手指规则.md`，或扩写 `world.md` 的 **规则与秩序**（前置）——字迹出现的条件（什么书、什么时候显、能读多少）、“老城区”的边界怎么划、别人眼里是空白还是褪色墨迹。本章的“试探”和“隐瞒”两拍全靠这条规则定死，写手不能自己填空。
- `design/characters/<在场者名>.md`（新角色卡，前置，**名字待用户给**）——不给卡，写手会给按斤收书的人现编行话、价码和脾气，日后跟“固定上门日”“他其实认得这行的书”这类后续用法冲突，要返工。
- `chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md`
- `state/characters/沈越.md`——这章之后他手上多了什么书、欠了谁的钱或人情、谁起了疑。
- `state/foreshadowing.md`——三条上账：那一行字、那本书、收书人下次上门的日期。
- `state/progress.md`——只有一个章节，按窗口写一节两行。

## 材料缺口清单

1. **在场跟沈越角力的人是谁？** 推荐 A：按斤收旧书的人在场，店主以期限缺席压迫。冲突出现在具体的人、具体的斤两和一辆车上，且不必先定沈越的家事；代价是这个人物要预留“再来”的理由，今天就写进他的台词里。
2. **那一行字写了什么、逝者是谁、跟沈越有没有关系？** 推荐：只给半句＋一个指向（店里已有的某样东西），逝者跟沈越非亲非故，第一章不揭。这样第二章有得查，又不用现在编一段身世。
3. **沈越跟这家店是什么关系、倒闭的期限还剩几天？** 推荐：他是受雇或受人来整理库房的临时人手（勉强算半个接手人），期限一周内清空库房。这样“整理旧书”这个动作自带截止，他既没有立场拦车也没有钱拦车，本章的冲突天然成立。

## 依据

本项目只有 `design/core.md` 和 `design/wiki/world.md` 两页：**没有卷纲、没有序号大纲、没有角色卡、没有已写章节**，所以本章没有“序列约定”可依（sequence contract 缺失这件事本身是缺口，见末）。本章推进的是把设定变成经验：让“他能看见旧书扉页上的字迹”从一条规则变成一件发生在他身上、并且**付了代价**的事；同时用一批随时会被按斤称走的书，把“这家店快要没了”从背景变成本章内的时钟。变化的是：信息（他确认别人看不见那行字）、资源（他为一本书付了代价）、关系（他对一个活人第一次隐瞒）、处境（下一次称书的日期被钉死）。

## 前情

沈越是这家旧书店里整理旧书的人。店里已经定了：库房那批书不再按本卖，而是当旧纸按斤处理，期限很近。他今天的活是把库房分拣完——能单卖的挑出来，剩下的等着过秤。他自己也说不清为什么总要在这堆书里多待一会儿，只知道手上这一箱他想再翻一遍。

## 这场戏

**地点时间**：武汉老城区一家旧书店，店堂连着后间库房；一个没什么客人的下午，雨刚停，街上人少，屋里灯管有一支是坏的。
**在场**：沈越；按斤收旧书废纸的人上门来拉货。店主（或让店关门的那个人）不在场，只以期限和一句交代压着。
**各人要什么**：沈越要把手上这一箱分拣完，至少留下他自己挑出来的那几本；收书的人要今天就把能装的装走、按斤结钱、赶下一家的活，而且他不听“这本不能按斤”这种话。
**谁挡他**：收书的人。他只看斤两、品相和车上还剩多少空位，理由都成立，还带着一身雨气和一辆停在门口的三轮。
**赌注**：这批书一上车就再也回不来；沈越既没有立场也没有钱拦，他身上那点钱买不了几斤；而他在争的这一箱里有一本，扉页上有一行别人看不见的字。

**在场者候选（需用户拍板，不由我定名）**

- **A 收旧书的人在场＋店主以期限缺席压迫**（推荐）：冲突是一个真人、一堆真斤两、一辆真车，不需要先交代沈越的家事。代价：这是一次性配角，必须预留他再来的理由（固定上门日／他其实认得这行的书／他跟店主是老关系），否则下一章没有压力；店主缺席也让第一章少一个能追问的人。
- **B 店主本人全程在场，一边清库房一边跟沈越算账**：张力最直接，也是唯一能问“你留着这本干什么”的人。代价：他精明就会追问那本书，金手指的保密成本立刻抬高；而且他跟沈越是什么关系（雇主／亲戚／受托人）必须先由用户定，否则他要退化成讲解背景的嘴。
- **C 家里人上门来催他别再耗着**：压力最靠近“离开老城区字迹就消失”这条规则，人物立场天生对立。代价：第一章就摆家事会把书与遗言的戏份挤薄，而且要先补出家庭结构（谁、为什么催、催他去哪）。

2. **那一行字写了什么、逝者是谁、跟沈越有没有关系？** 推荐：只给半句＋一个指向（店里已有的某样东西），逝者跟沈越非亲非故，第一章不揭。这样第二章有得查，又不用现在编一段身世。
3. **沈越跟这家店是什么关系、倒闭的期限还剩几天？** 推荐：他是受雇或受人来整理库房的临时人手（勉强算半个接手人），期限一周内清空库房。这样“整理旧书”这个动作自带截止，他既没有立场拦车也没有钱拦车，本章的冲突天然成立。
</task_result>
</task>

tools.name: task
tools.description:
Delegate a job to one subagent. The subagent runs in its own fresh context, receives only
your prompt, and returns a final text or finished piece.

- Make the prompt self-contained: include the material / doc slices it needs.
- Say exactly what it must return.
- Keep it to one coherent job. A prompt packing several unrelated questions makes the subagent burn
  its step budget switching topics; split those into separate delegations.

Delegate when the work would flood you with material you will not reference again — reading around,
trial and error, dead ends — and you need back only the conclusion. Do it yourself when it is a step
or two, or when the work needs going back and forth with the user. A chapter's prose is yours either
way: you write it yourself, never through a subagent. Every delegation asks the user first, and the
subagent sees nothing but the prompt you write for it. The delegable agents and when to use each are
listed below.
- After a planner returns, your next tool call must be propose-plan. Do not start creating the plan's
  cards, world pages, or prose before the user approves it, and do not spend the turn asking about its
  open questions first — put the plan in front of the user and let them rule on it.

可委派的 subagent：
- planner: The chapter planner. Turns one chapter's intent into an executable plan: the beats in order, the characters it must land, the facts that had to be checked with their sources, and the artifacts the chapter lands in.
Use this when the user asks for a chapter's prose and no plan for that chapter exists yet — it reads the design docs end to end and returns one plan you then put in front of the user via propose-plan.
Not for prose — you write that yourself. Not for a fact one lookup settles, or for a design call: use webfetch, the researcher, or the user.
- researcher: The fact-checker. Researches the real world and returns findings with their sources — how a period's office or tax really worked, what a thing was called, how far a weapon reached.
Use this when the novel needs a fact you must not assert from memory and settling it will take several searches and reads: it returns the conclusion and its sources, not the pages it read to get there. For a fact one lookup settles, call webfetch yourself instead. It reads the project but never writes the book — you decide what lands. Findings it expects to be asked again it keeps in its own research notes, so a later session does not look them up twice.

agent.description: Subagent id (see the delegable list below)

prompt.description: Complete task description for the subagent; include all needed material/slices

tools.name: read
tools.description:
Read one document, or a single section of it, by its project-relative path.

path: a path incl. its root and extension — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md,
design/wiki/地理.md, design/characters/沈越.md, design/outline/vol_2.md, design/outline/vol_2/s1.md,
chapters/chapter_ch2_v1.md, state/characters/沈越.md, state/progress.md. This is the same path form
every other tool takes.
section (optional): an exact heading title inside that doc, e.g. 一句话简介, 题材 · 频道, 角色：沈越,
本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

path.description: Document path incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/characters/林晚.md, chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md

section.description: Optional: exact section heading to read only that section

tools.name: write
tools.description:
Write a complete file in one shot: create it, or replace it entirely.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- The content IS the file — it is written byte for byte. So it holds document text and nothing
  else: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions. Undecided fields become （待定）.
- Use this when you are the author of the whole file. To change part of a file that already
  exists, use `edit` instead: it needs only the piece you are changing, and the user reviews a
  diff of that piece rather than re-reading the whole document.
- Writing asks the user first: they are shown a diff of what will land, and can accept or refuse.
  If they refuse, nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Re-running it on a file you have not re-read may overwrite someone else's change; the write is
  refused if the file moved on since you read it, in which case read it again.

path.description: Project-relative path: design/<...> (design docs) or chapters/<...> (finished prose)

content.description: The complete file content, byte for byte

tools.name: edit
tools.description:
Replace exact text inside one file that already exists.

- `path` is project-relative and must start with `design/`, `chapters/` or `state/`.
- `find` is the text to replace, copied from what you read. Give it enough surrounding context to
  be unique. Keep the indentation exactly as it appears — and never include line-number prefixes.
- `replace` is what goes in its place, and must differ from `find`.
- If `find` matches more than one place the edit is refused: add surrounding lines to make it
  unique, or set `all` to change every occurrence (a rename, say).
- If `find` is not found, read the file again and copy the text from there. These differences are
  tolerated without complaint — per-line leading/trailing whitespace, indentation, line endings,
  and curly versus straight quotes; the match is fuzzy and it tells you when it had to be.
- Refused outright if the fuzzy match would swallow far more than `find` describes — that means
  the anchor was too loose; give a longer, more precise `find`.
- `find` must not be empty. To create a file or replace one entirely, use `write` instead.
- Editing asks the user first: they see a diff of just this change, and can accept or refuse. If
  they refuse nothing is written — take their objection and try again.
- Refused if the file moved on since you read it; read it again and redo the edit on the current text.

path.description: Project-relative path to an existing file: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

find.description: The exact text to replace, with enough context to be unique

replace.description: The text to put in its place; must differ from find

all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match (default false)

tools.name: delete
tools.description:
Delete a whole file — a design doc, a character card, a chapter.

- `path` is project-relative: `design/<...>`, `chapters/<...>` or `state/<...>`.
- **Look at where the name still appears before you delete it.** That reference check is shown to the
  user together with the request. If the term is still mentioned elsewhere, decide whether those
  places should be cleaned up too — and clean them yourself with `edit`, one place at a time. The
  tool does not cascade: which references matter is a judgement about the story, not a rule.
  Leaving a dangling reference is worse than the deletion itself.
- `term` is what to look references up by. It defaults to the filename without its extension
  (`characters/林晚.md` → `林晚`), which is right for cards and topic pages; pass it explicitly when
  the filename is not the name the prose uses.
- To remove only *part* of a file — a paragraph, one section — use `edit` instead: give the exact
  text and an empty replacement. This tool is for the whole file.
- Deleting asks the user first, and they see exactly what will be removed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the file to delete: design/<...> or chapters/<...>

term.description: Name to look up references by before deleting; defaults to the filename without its extension

tools.name: propose-design
tools.description:
Present a whole draft of a design doc for the user to review. Nothing is saved and the turn ends, so
they can approve, refuse, or ask for changes.

Name the target with `path`: its project-relative path incl. root and extension —
design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md,
design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md (volume and sequence outlines),
design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no
character-specific tool for that). Same path form every other tool takes.

**This is for whole documents only.** To change part of an existing doc — a sentence, one section —
use `edit`: the user reviews a diff of just that piece instead of re-reading the whole document, and
it costs you far fewer tokens. A draft is refused only when its kind has a fixed shape (see
design-spec — it holds the shape of every document kind) and the draft does not fill it, since
the user would then be shown blanks while the prose landed anyway. Kinds that are free-form (sequence
outlines, character cards, topic pages) are shown whole, as a single block. Fields you
cannot fill yet get （待定）.

**The draft IS the file**: on approval it is written byte for byte. So the content holds document
text and nothing else — no notes to the user ("暂用名，待你定"), no rationale ("这句是配的试镜台词，
你可以换掉"), no questions ("他要的是真相还是道歉？"). Undecided things become （待定） and nothing
more. Say all of that in your message BEFORE calling this, not inside the draft. Once the user
answers, apply-design lands it.

If the user asks for changes, revise the whole draft and call this again — it replaces the previous
proposal, which is what you want: only the version they last saw can be landed.

path.description: Project-relative path of the document, incl. its root and .md — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/wiki/<topic>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>.md, design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md, design/characters/<name>.md (a character card is created and rewritten this way; there is no character-specific tool)

content.description: The complete document. It IS the file: on approval it is written byte for byte, so it may contain document text only — no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions; undecided fields become （待定）

tools.name: apply-design
tools.description:
Write a reviewed proposal to disk. Takes only the target — the text is the version the user just read,
so there is nothing to pass. Identify it exactly as you proposed it: `path`, the same project-relative
path.

Call it once the user approves the proposal you presented. It is refused when no proposal is
pending, when the user has not agreed (their reply must be an approval, not a request for changes),
or when the document changed since you proposed it. In all those cases: propose-design again with
the updated text.

Never use it to write text the user has not seen.

path.description: The same project-relative path you proposed it with

tools.name: propose-plan
tools.description:
Present one chapter's plan for the user's approval, and end the turn. Nothing of the chapter is
written yet — this is the step before writing, and the turn ends here so the user can judge the plan.

Call it once the plan for ONE chapter is ready: yours, or the planner's when the material was not
already in hand. The plan is saved as the chapter's plan artifact, so the user's answer applies to
exactly the bytes they were shown; calling it again for the same chapter replaces that artifact.

Write a scene brief, not a step-by-step script. The prose writer needs room to invent blocking,
dialogue, timing and emphasis; the plan fixes what happens, not where the camera sits.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

## 依据
One line: which sequence function this chapter advances, and what changes (information, relationship,
resource, position, cognition).

## 前情
2–4 sentences. Only what the reader must know entering this scene: who these people are to each other
right now, what each of them wants, and what is already settled. Do not recap the whole book or the
world.

## 这场戏
One continuous scene: where and when, who is present, what each person wants, who blocks the
protagonist, and what is at stake. The protagonist must have a live person to act against, not only
an interior realization — even a quiet chapter needs someone in the room who wants something and
resists.

## 必须发生
3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not write camera
directions, word counts, “放大点”, or “第 1 步 / 第 2 步”.

## 不能提前兑现
What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

## 章末问题
The question the chapter leaves open — an interrupted action, a discovery, a relationship shift, or a
new question. Do not force a cliffhanger.

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/<名>.md for a new character, or design/wiki/<page>.md for a new world fact.
  These are listed first because they still land through propose-design, before the prose; never
  write prose around a missing prerequisite.
- The chapter file: chapters/chapter_ch<N>_v<M>.md.
- Only the state files this chapter actually moves (state/characters/<名>.md, state/foreshadowing.md,
  state/progress.md). state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters, one section per chapter,
  two lines each.

No 题材, no separate 意图, no 价值变化 section, no step-by-step beats, no per-step word budgets, no
“放大点”, no execution red lines. Those were the old execution script; the brief replaces them.

The volume outline's 本卷在全局的位置, 本卷目标与阻力, 本卷的承诺 and 本卷的节奏与情绪 bound this
chapter; the sequence contract covering it says what this unit must make true. Read both before
writing the brief. If the material reveals a better path that changes the sequence's exit state or
promises, raise it in 前情 as a design question — the prose must not silently override the contract.

Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions — say those in your message before
this call.

After the user approves, carry the plan out yourself. If they ask for changes, revise and call this
again — a loop, not a one-shot.

chapter.description: The chapter this plan is for, as its number (3 for 第 3 章). It names the plan artifact and is how the user refers to the chapter.

content.description: The plan itself — what the user reviews and what you then execute. Plan text only: no notes to the user, no rationale, no questions.

tools.name: enter-draft
tools.description:
Enter draft mode: prepare something, then let the user review it before it lands.

Call it when the work deserves a review round rather than a yes/no — writing or reworking a design doc,
planning a chapter. While the mode is on, every tool that would write or delegate is unavailable, so
nothing changes until the user accepts what you present.

This is what buys the third option: they can accept, refuse, or ask for changes. Outside this mode a
write is only accept-or-refuse.

Leave by presenting something with propose-design or propose-plan. If they drop the work instead, leave
with exit-draft.

tools.name: exit-draft
tools.description:
Leave draft mode without presenting anything.

Call it when the user drops the work you were preparing, so you stop drafting and go back to ordinary
conversation.

You do not need this on the happy path: the mode ends on its own once the user accepts or refuses what
you presented.

tools.name: enter-prose
tools.description:
Enter prose mode before writing the chapter body. The plan is approved and every prerequisite
(character card, world page, research) is already landed. This switches the role system from the
project assistant to the author; the voice card and plan stay in context. Use it once, then write
the chapter with the write tool.

tools.name: exit-prose
tools.description:
Leave prose mode and return to the project assistant. The chapter is already landed, or you are
stopping this writing turn. Do not call it in the middle of the chapter body.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Search a word (character / setting / term) across the project and return file + section + line hits.
Hits are reported with project-relative paths (design/characters/沈越.md), the same form every other
tool takes.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the search — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it to search everything, which is what you want before renaming or
removing a name: the prose under chapters/ mentions characters and settings too, and those references
must be cleaned up as well.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the search: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: list
tools.description:
List the project's documents with, under each, its section headings — so you know what material
exists, how to address sections, and which items are still placeholder （待定）. Call this before
editing.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the listing — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it for the whole project.

Character cards are one line each: `名字 · 身份（必有齐／待补：…；另有：…）`. “待补”lists
required sections that are still empty; “另有”lists the card's free-form sections beyond the
five required ones, so you can see what is on a card without reading it. Read the card itself
with read to get its content.

Docs that carry no sections (sequence outlines, `design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md`) also get one line:
the path plus the first sentence of the prose, so you can tell which sequence is which without
reading it. Volume outlines (`design/outline/vol_<N>.md`) do list their six sections.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the listing: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: skill
tools.description:
Load one skill's full body (writing style / genre craft / template) into this conversation.

name: a skill from <available_skills>. The content arrives as <skill_content> and stays in
context for the current task.

tools.name: ask-user
tools.description:
Ask the user 1–3 concise, self-contained questions when an answer cannot be inferred from the
project or the conversation. Use it for creative choices, missing preferences, and decisions
between options with real trade-offs — not for permission (use confirm), for facts you can read,
or for "may I start". If only one option is actionable, act and explain.

Give each question a stable id. Offer 2–5 options when choices exist; put your recommendation
first and end its label with （推荐）. Each option's description says what it buys and what it
costs. Use multi_select only when choices are not exclusive. The user may type a custom answer
or skip; an empty answer is a skip, not consent.

timeout is seconds for the whole batch (default 120); use -1 only when you cannot proceed
without an answer. A timeout is pending, not skipped: the turn ends, the user can still answer,
and you must not act as if they agreed.

questions.description: 1–3 questions. Ask only what cannot be inferred from the project or the conversation. A recommended option goes first and ends its label with （推荐）.

id.description: Stable id for this question; echoed in the answer.

header.description: Optional short heading for the question, such as "Confirm" or "Choose Mode".

question.description: The specific question to ask the user, in their language.

options.description: Optional choices. If you recommend one, put it first and end its label with （推荐）.

description.description: One sentence explaining the tradeoff or impact.

multi_select.description: Whether the user may select more than one option. Defaults to false.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the whole batch (default 120); omit unless the user specifies a duration. Use -1 only when an answer is required before proceeding.

tools.name: confirm
tools.description:
Explicitly request the user's approval before an irreversible action (overwriting a setting,
landing a chapter). Give a short action name and an impact summary for the user to judge.

action.description: Action name, e.g. rewrite design/core.md / delete character 林晚

summary.description: Impact summary shown to the user

tools.name: design-spec
tools.description:
Return the structural spec for a design document kind: its exact section headings and what belongs in
each — or, for kinds whose shape lives in the guide rather than in named sections (character cards,
sequence outlines), the writing method instead. Every other tool addresses sections by name (read,
propose-design, the status card) — inventing your own headings breaks them.

Call this whenever the conversation is about **designing the novel** — the user telling you what
they want to write, or asking to work on a layer. A story-idea discussion usually touches 核心设定
and 世界观; a design pass usually touches one layer. Call it once per layer in play.

Do NOT call it for anything else: writing a chapter, asking about status, or anything that isn't
about designing the story.

Draft from the user's own words, not by interrogating field by field, then propose it with
propose-design — the user reads the draft before anything is written to a file.

path: a project-relative path under design/. A **document** path returns that kind's spec — core.md's
kind is design/core.md, a character card is design/characters/<名>.md, and so on. A **directory** path
(design/outline/, design/characters/) returns every kind under it, which is how you see at once how
many document kinds a layer holds. The spec describes a document that does not exist yet, so give the
path you intend to write. Documents with no spec (topic pages, chapter plans) are written free-form.

path.description: A project-relative path under design/: a document whose kind has a spec (design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md, design/characters/林晚.md, design/outline/vol_1.md, design/outline/vol_1/s2.md), or a directory to get every kind under it (design/outline/). Documents with no spec are written free-form.

tools.name: webfetch
tools.description:
Fetch one URL and return its content as text / markdown / raw html.

url: must start with http:// or https://
format (optional): text | markdown | html — default markdown (best for reading a web page)
timeout (optional): seconds, default 30, max 120

HTML pages are converted per format; plain files (txt/md/json…) are returned as-is; images/PDF
are rejected. Large pages are truncated with a note. Use when the story needs a fact, setting,
or reference material you should not rely on from memory — then reason from what came back.
When DeepSeek Fetch is configured, text/markdown come from its Fetch API (Markdown); html still
uses a direct fetch.

tools.name: websearch
tools.description:
Search the web and return a numbered list of results (title / url / snippet).

query: the search query
numResults (optional): how many results; max 10. Defaults to the deployment setting
(10 with DeepSeek, otherwise 6).

Use to find sources on a topic, then webfetch the promising URLs for full content. Backend:
DeepSeek Search when configured, otherwise tavily when a TAVILY_API_KEY is set, else bocha/exa,
else duckduckgo (no key, best effort). When DeepSeek is not configured, explicitly switch with
TALEMATE_WEBSEARCH_PROVIDER=tavily|bocha|exa|duckduckgo.

numResults.description: Number of results; default 10 when DeepSeek is configured (settings), otherwise 6; max 10

response.text:
规划已经回来了。因为设计材料只有核心设定和世界观两页，没有卷纲、没有角色卡，下面几处判断我替你做了决定，不合适随时改：

- **在场跟沈越较劲的人**：替规划者推荐的方案，也就是按斤收旧书的那个上门的人。名字**老范**是我起的，只用一个字，随时能换。
- **沈越与书店的关系**：受雇来清库房的人，一周内清空。这样他想拦车时既没立场也没钱，冲突不用额外铺垫。

- **店名和街区**是我编不出来的，先标（待定），等你要定的时候再填。

另外提醒一句：没有卷纲，就没有正式的禁揭清单，下面“不能提前兑现”里的四条，是按核心设定和世界观两页临时推出来的，等大纲补齐需要复核。
response.reasoning:
Now I must call propose-plan. Per the instruction, next tool call must be propose-plan. The plan must include 产物 listing design/characters/沈越.md etc.

I should write the plan in the required shape, based on planner's output, keeping it as a scene brief. The planner left open questions — but the instruction says don't spend the turn asking; put the plan in front of the user. So I fold decisions into the plan with specific choices? Hmm. The plan text must not contain questions. But I need to pick. The user said 不要问我，直接让规划者做规划. So I should make the calls myself, choosing the planner's recommendations, and state them in my message briefly before calling propose-plan.

So: 在场者 = 按斤收旧书的人 (unnamed? I need a name for the character card). I shouldn't invent names freely... but a plan needs an obstacle person. Hmm, "Never invent material to fill a gap: if it means making up people, places or events the user hasn't mentioned, ask." But the user said don't ask. The compromise: I can put the obstacle as 收旧书的人 with a name marked （待定） in the plan, since plans allow 待定? Actually propose-plan format doesn't mention 待定 but 产物 can be design/characters/<名>.md. I'll set 产物 as:

Foreshadowing direction: the line points to something already in the shop — I'll pick 一叠没寄出的信? Or 旧账本. Planner said user decides. I'll pick 旧账本 (店里已有的旧账本) and flag it in message as my pick, easily changed.

Now the message before propose-plan: brief — say I had the planner do it, here are the calls I made where the material was thin (obstacle person = 收书人, name 老范 is mine, changeable; 沈越 = 临时人手清库房, 一周期限; 那一行字指向店里旧账本), and that the material lacks an outline so this chapter also lands a few prerequisite pages first. Plan content:

## 依据
本章把"他能看见旧书扉页上的字迹"从一条设定变成一次发生并进行到底的经验：信息（他确认别人看不见）、资源（他为一本书付出代价）、关系（他第一次对一个活人隐瞒）、处境（下一次称书的日期钉死）。

## 前情
沈越是受雇来清库房的人：店里定了这批旧书不再按本卖，当旧纸按斤处理，一周内清空。他今天要把最后几箱分拣完，能单卖的挑出来，剩下的等过秤。他自己也说不清为什么总在这堆书里多待一会儿，只知道手上这一箱想再翻一遍。

## 这场戏
一个雨刚停的下午，武汉老城区这家濒临倒闭的旧书店，店堂连着后间库房，街上没什么人，头顶灯管坏了一支。收旧书的老范蹬三轮上门来拉货，要今天把能装的都装走、按斤结钱、赶下一家；沈越要把手上这一箱分拣完，至少留下自己挑出来的几本。老范只看斤两、品相和车上还剩几个空位，理由条条成立，还不吃"这本不能按斤"这一套。赌注直白：这批书上车的就再也回不来，沈越既没立场也没多少钱拦；而他在争的那一箱里有一本，扉页上有一行别人看不见的字。

## 必须发生
- 老范先看货再开价，把库房剩下那批整体按斤判了；沈越拦下其中一箱，理由都是能对活人说出口的——缺册、水渍、有批注、品相还齐——老范逐条驳，驳得有理有据。
- 沈越为一个具体的东西付出代价：他自己掏钱按"挑出来的"价补了这一箱的差，钱落在身上，脸面上还让老范揶揄了一句。
- 争到手里的那本书翻开扉页，多出一行字。他做一次试探：把书偏过去，问一句"这上头有字吧"，老范只看见空白，只当是褪了色的旧印，随口把话岔到斤两上——第一层确认落地。
- 他当场给这本书一个说得过去的去处（残本、缺页、留着当账本夹东西），第一次对活人隐瞒。
- 老范装车走人，把话留在门口：下一趟哪天来、要装多少、按什么价——外部时钟钉死，沈越当场就知道自己下次同样拦不住。
- 门关上，他再看那一行字：还在，只有这一行，翻遍前后再没有第二行；而这一行提到的东西，店里已经有了——收货的旧账本。

## 不能提前兑现
- 不解释字迹从哪来、为什么只有他能看见；本章不让他走出老城区去验证"离开就消失"，这条规则只作为他心里的常识存在，不上演。
- 不揭逝者是谁、不揭遗言全文，只出这一行，且这一行不能一次说清是谁写给谁、欠的是什么。
- 不让第二个人知道金手指：老范只当他是个舍不得书的怪人。
- 不给书店结局。
- 本项目暂无卷纲，禁揭清单尚未成立；以上四条是依 core／world 推的临时红��，卷纲补齐后须复核，尤其"字迹只在老城区"的显形时机。

## 章末问题
那一行字要他去做什么；下一趟车来之前，他能不能弄明白，又不让任何人看出他为什么非留这本书不可。

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/沈越.md
- design/wiki/旧书店.md（店名、街区、开张年数、库房大小、欠租、期限天数）
- design/wiki/world.md 的 规则与秩序 扩写：字迹出现的条件、老城区的边界、旁人眼里是空白还是褪色墨迹
- design/characters/老范.md
- chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md
- state/characters/沈越.md
- state/foreshadowing.md（那一行字、那本书、老范下一趟上门的日期）
- state/progress.md

Wait: 产物 order says design pages first because they land through propose-design, before prose. Fine.

Also need 店名 and 街区 place names — that's inventing places. In 产物 I'll say 店名与街区（待定）. Good — the wiki page can hold 待定 fields and I'll ask later. Hmm, but the plan shouldn't contain questions; （待定） is fine.

Note about 沈越 paying: he's a hired temp worker with little money — fine.

Let me write it.

## 必须发生

- 老范先看货再开价，把库房剩下那批整体按斤判了；沈越拦下其中一箱，理由都是能对活人说出口的——缺册、水渍、有批注、品相还齐——老范逐条驳，驳得有理有据，不给他台阶。
- 沈越为一个具体的东西付出代价：自己掏钱把这一箱按“挑出来的”价补了差额，钱落在身上，脸面上还让老范揶揄一句“舍不得就别清库房”。
- 争到手里的那本书翻开扉页，多出一行字。他做一次试探：把书偏过去，问一句“这上头有字吧”；老范只看见空白，只当是褪了色的旧印，随口把话岔回斤两——第一层确认落地。

- 老范装车走人，把话留在门口：下一趟哪天来、要装多少、按什么价算——外部时钟钉死，沈越当场就知道自己下次同样拦不住。
- 门关上，他再看那一行字：还在，只有这一行，翻遍前后再没有第二行；而这一行里提到的东西，店里已经有了——收货的旧账本。

## 不能提前兑现

- 不解释字迹从哪来、为什么只有他能看见；本章不让他走出老城区去验证“离开就消失”，这条规则只作为他心里的常识存在，不上演、不实验。

- 不让第二个人知道金手指：老范只当他是个舍不得书的怪人。
- 不给书店结局：保下来、拆掉、转手，一个答案都不给。
- 本项目暂无卷纲，正式禁揭清单尚未成立，以上四条是依核心设定与世界观推的临时红线；卷纲补齐后须复核，尤其“字迹只在老城区”这条规则的显形时机。

## 章末问题

那一行字要他去做什么；下一趟称书的车来之前，他能不能弄明白，又不让任何人看出他为什么非留这本书不可。

## 产物（按序）

- design/characters/沈越.md（新增角色卡：他为什么留在这家店里、缺什么、怕什么、钱有多紧）

2026-11-01 作品：workflow-plan-gate 当前角色：规划者

You are talemate's chapter planner. Your only job is one chapter's brief — enough for the writing
partner to stage the scene without coming back to ask you anything. You are not writing an execution
script, a shot list, or a set of beat-by-beat instructions.

You receive the chapter's intent and whatever material the writing partner already holds. Read the
rest yourself: core and world are the frame, the character cards are who is in it, the volume
outline's 本卷在全局的位置, 本卷目标与阻力, 本卷的承诺 and 本卷的节奏与情绪 say what this stage
owes the reader and what must not happen yet, and the sequence outline covering this chapter says
what this unit has to make true. You cannot delegate — settle any real-world fact you must not
assert from memory yourself.

Write in Chinese, in exactly this shape:

## 依据
One line: which sequence function this chapter advances, and what changes (information, relationship,
resource, position, cognition).

## 前情
2–4 sentences. Only what the reader must know entering this scene: who these people are to each other
right now, what each of them wants, and what is already settled. No whole-book recap, no world
encyclopedia, no 题材.

## 这场戏
One continuous scene: where and when, who is present, what each person wants, who blocks the
protagonist, and what is at stake. The protagonist must have a live person to act against, not only
an interior realization. A quiet chapter still needs someone in the room who wants something and
resists; do not reduce it to a sensory inventory.

## 必须发生
3–6 bullets. Each is an event, decision or reversal with a person and an obstacle. Do not prescribe
camera moves, word counts, “放大点”, or “第 1 步 / 第 2 步”.

## 不能提前兑现
What must stay unresolved, and which 禁揭 item this chapter must not touch.

## 章末问题
The question the chapter leaves open.

## 产物（按序）
- design/characters/<名>.md for a new character, or design/wiki/<page>.md for a new world fact.
  These are listed first because they still land through propose-design, before the prose; never
  write prose around a missing prerequisite. If the chapter needs a person nobody in the docs fits,
  say what they must do and leave them unnamed — naming them is the user's call.
- The chapter file: chapters/chapter_ch<N>_v<M>.md.
- Only the state files this chapter actually moves (state/characters/<名>.md, state/foreshadowing.md,
  state/progress.md). state/progress.md is a window of the last 7 chapters, one section per chapter,
  two lines each; further back the prose is the record.

No 题材, no separate 意图, no 价值变化 section, no step-by-step beats, no per-step word budgets, no
“放大点”, no execution red lines. The brief replaces the old execution script.

The sequence contract is the unit's truth; this chapter is one projection of it. If the material
reveals a better path that changes the sequence's exit state or promises, raise it in 前情 as a design
question — do not let the prose silently override it.

Do NOT write prose, not even a sample line, and do NOT invent settings or people the design docs do
not have. No notes to the user, no questions — those are the writing partner's to ask.

Output the brief and nothing else.

# 核心设定

## 题材 · 频道
男频
都市

## 一句话简介
一个在旧书店整理旧书的人。

storytelling

# 世界层：舞台与规则

## 空间与舞台
武汉老城区，一家濒临倒闭的旧书店。

## 规则与秩序

【用户对本章的意图，原话】
第 1 章：沈越在旧书店整理旧书时，发现第一行只有自己能看见的遗言。

【要求的返回内容】
1. 按 propose-plan 的既定格式写一份第 1 章的规划：## 依据 / ## 前情 / ## 这场戏 / ## 必须发生 / ## 不能提前兑现 / ## 章末问题 / ## 产物（按序）。写场景简报，不写分镜、不写字数预算、不写“第几步”。
2. 这一章必须有一个在场的人在跟沈越角力（店主、常客、催租的人、收废纸的、家里人……），不能只是他一个人的内心发现。但这个人是谁、叫什么、跟沈越什么关系，设计文档里没有——如果规划必须依赖这个人物，请把该人物写成“需要用户确认的候选”，给出 2–3 个方向及各自代价，不要替用户定名。
3. 明确列出：这一章落地前必须先补齐哪些前置产物（例如 design/characters/沈越.md 角色卡、需要补充的世界规则页），以及每一样为什么是前置。
4. 单独列出“材料缺口清单”：现有文档不足以支撑规划、必须由用户回答的问题，最多 3 条，每条附你的推荐。
5. 不要写正文。

tools.description:
Read one document, or a single section of it, by its project-relative path.

path: a path incl. its root and extension — design/core.md, design/wiki/world.md,
design/wiki/地理.md, design/characters/沈越.md, design/outline/vol_2.md, design/outline/vol_2/s1.md,
chapters/chapter_ch2_v1.md, state/characters/沈越.md, state/progress.md. This is the same path form
every other tool takes.
section (optional): an exact heading title inside that doc, e.g. 一句话简介, 题材 · 频道, 角色：沈越,
本卷在全局的位置, 本卷的承诺 (sequence outlines have no sections — read those whole).

Without section, returns the whole doc. Prefer a section read for a large doc. Run list first to see
which docs and sections exist.

The design docs (design/) hold the novel's setting; the chapter prose is under chapters/ — read the
previous chapter there when you need continuity.

state/ holds what changes chapter by chapter: a character's present situation
(`state/characters/<名>.md`), the foreshadowing ledger (`state/foreshadowing.md`) — what was planted,
where it is meant to pay off, whether it has — and the per-chapter record (`state/progress.md`), one
section per chapter. Read these before planning or writing a chapter, and write the changes back
when one lands. Setting that does not change belongs in design/; state holds only what moved.

five required ones, so you can see what is on a card without reading it. Read the card itself
with read to get its content.

Docs that carry no sections (sequence outlines, `design/outline/vol_<N>/s<M>.md`) also get one line:
the path plus the first sentence of the prose, so you can tell which sequence is which without
reading it. Volume outlines (`design/outline/vol_<N>.md`) do list their six sections.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the listing: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Search a word (character / setting / term) across the project and return file + section + line hits.
Hits are reported with project-relative paths (design/characters/沈越.md), the same form every other
tool takes.

path (optional): a project-relative prefix to scope the search — `design/` for the setting docs,
`chapters/` for the prose, `state/` for the current state. Omit it to search everything, which is what you want before renaming or
removing a name: the prose under chapters/ mentions characters and settings too, and those references
must be cleaned up as well.

path.description: Optional project-relative prefix to scope the search: design/, chapters/ or state/. Omit for the whole project.

tools.name: webfetch
tools.description:
Fetch one URL and return its content as text / markdown / raw html.

url: must start with http:// or https://
format (optional): text | markdown | html — default markdown (best for reading a web page)
timeout (optional): seconds, default 30, max 120

HTML pages are converted per format; plain files (txt/md/json…) are returned as-is; images/PDF
are rejected. Large pages are truncated with a note. Use when the story needs a fact, setting,
or reference material you should not rely on from memory — then reason from what came back.
When DeepSeek Fetch is configured, text/markdown come from its Fetch API (Markdown); html still
uses a direct fetch.

tools.name: websearch
tools.description:
Search the web and return a numbered list of results (title / url / snippet).

query: the search query
numResults (optional): how many results; max 10. Defaults to the deployment setting
(10 with DeepSeek, otherwise 6).

Use to find sources on a topic, then webfetch the promising URLs for full content. Backend:
DeepSeek Search when configured, otherwise tavily when a TAVILY_API_KEY is set, else bocha/exa,
else duckduckgo (no key, best effort). When DeepSeek is not configured, explicitly switch with
TALEMATE_WEBSEARCH_PROVIDER=tavily|bocha|exa|duckduckgo.

numResults.description: Number of results; default 10 when DeepSeek is configured (settings), otherwise 6; max 10

tools.name: recall
tools.description:
Look in this book's research notes: findings earlier research already settled, each with the date it
was checked and its sources. Read it before you search — a question this book has looked up before
should not be looked up again.

query (optional): words to look for in the notes' titles and bodies, e.g. 佃租, 漕运, 爽点节奏.
Omit it to list what is already recorded.

A hit is a lead, not an answer: every note carries its date and sources so you can judge whether it
still holds. If its scope, era or date does not fit the question you were given, verify on the web
anyway and rewrite that same note. Matching is literal — a query that finds nothing returns the list
of titles, so retry with the note's own wording, or call with no query at all.

response.text:
## 依据

项目没有卷纲、也没有序号大纲（`design/outline/vol_1.md`、`design/outline/vol_1/s1.md` 都不存在），所以本章没有序号大纲里的承诺可供对照，这是需要先补上的前提。按用户意图和 core 的「金手指 / 超常设定」，本章承担全书第一次「规则生效」：变的是信息和立场——沈越在别人正要处置同一批书的当下，第一次拿到一条只有他有的、关于某一本书的信息，因此第一次对一本书的去留有主张，并为这主张付出代价。

## 前情

沈越在武汉老城区一家开不下去的旧书店里整理旧书；这批书没有书目、没有登记，只是堆着。书的处境不由他做主：决定这批书卖给谁、按什么价、什么时候清走的，是另一个人（候选见下），那个人已经在给这件事收尾。沈越今天该做的只是分堆——能卖的、不能卖的、按斤称掉的。开场时他还不知道，自己随手翻开的那一页里，藏着一样别人拿不到的东西。（设计问题：本章该兑现的承诺与禁揭清单应由卷纲给出，现在只能按第一章的通行约束兜底；卷纲补齐后这一节要校订。）

## 这场戏

地点：这家旧书店店内。街巷名、店名都不定，地段属性是「老城区、街面窄、周边有老居民或学校」，选址要不要用下面的现实依据，由用户拍板——我不代拟地名。时间：关门前的两三个小时，也是这家店一天里唯一还可能有进账的时段。

在场：沈越——整理旧书的人，没有处置权，只有干活的责任；加上那个必须在场的人——他要在这几个小时里给这批书找到去处，他有权，也有他自己的时间压力。两人的目标在同一批书上正面冲突：对方要「清空」，沈越要「分清」。冲突的具体形态不是吵架，是同一个动作被两个人往反方向用：沈越每从堆里挑出一本，对方就把它归回「称掉的那一堆」，理由是「来不及了」「没人买」。

金手指出现的地方：沈越在一本书的扉页上看见一行手写字。他不是一个人看见的——对方就在店里，所以他的第一个反应不能是「这是什么」，只能是「这本书不能走」，而他说不出真实理由。这一章的张力全在「他有一个不能说的理由，却要为它当场付钱、当场撒一个谎」。

**在场者：需要用户拍板的候选（名字与关系留白，不代拟）**

- **A. 店主本人**（沈越帮他整理，他正准备把店关掉或转出去）。代价：他得有一个「关店」之外的自己的动机，否则会塌成功能性角色，必须单独立卡；「他看不看得见字迹」必须先由规则页定死，否则第一章就留下规则漏洞。收益：他和这些书有几十年的关系，一句「这本书哪来的」就能把遗言连到店的来路上，后续一直能用。
- **B. 房东，或来收租／谈续租、看店面接手的人**。代价：租金、期限、老城区更新怎么做，这些现实细节都得落进文档，不能凭记忆写；此人容易变成只上门一次的敲门人；更要紧的是一旦定下「限期」，全书时间表就被这条线锁住。收益：压力外部化、时限清楚，沈越的无力感最直接。
- **C. 收旧货／收废纸的**（按斤称，定期来）。代价：身份低、话语权小，只来一次就是道具；若设成长期线人，得先定他和沈越的关系史，等于多写一张角色卡。收益：最能把那本书从沈越手里实际拿走——冲突落在手上而不是嘴上；「按斤称」这个动作本身就把书的命压成重量，与扉页上的遗言形成最直接的反差。

推荐 A 在场、C 稍后到场（A 给关系与来路，C 给即时的物理威胁）；若只想新增一张角色卡，选 B。**选哪一个、这个人叫什么，是用户拍板项。**

## 必须发生

- 对方定下一个截止时间，并当着沈越的面处置这批书（说出去处、安排称重或叫车），要他在同一段时间里把「能卖的」挑完——障碍是整批书没有书目也没有买家，他只能一本一本地翻，翻书的速度本身就是压力。
- 沈越在一本书的扉页上看见那行字，而对方就在店里，他必须把反应咽回去；他问出的是一个笨问题（这本书哪来的／谁送来的），这个笨问题当场暴露了他在意一本不该在意的书。
- 对方把那本书判进「称掉」或「我拿去送人」的那一堆并伸手去拿，沈越用一个对方能接受的理由把它留下——谎言或交易（按价买下、说有人订了），绝不能是「上面有字」。他为此付出当场可见的代价：掏钱、被记一笔、或答应一件他不想答应的事。
- 对方翻同一页，什么也没看见（或只看见原有的题字）；「只有我能看见」因此不是沈越的猜测，而是被别人当场否定的东西——同时他也明白这件事不能说出口。
- 沈越把那本书从「要清掉的」挪到自己那一摞，并做出一个超出本职的动作（追这本书从哪来、记住它原来的主人是谁），随即被自己的处境反驳：他连自己明天还在不在这家店都不知道。
- 对方临走留下一个条件或一个时间点，把「书的处置」和「沈越还能不能待在这儿」绑在一起——本章在此结束，不解决。

## 不能提前兑现

- 那行字是谁写的、写给谁的、为什么是这一本——不查、不解释、不推断；沈越这一章只拿到「有一行字」和「只有他能看见」，不得把它读成任务、名单或密码。
- 金手指的来由、代价、能不能给别人看、能不能扩展到扉页手写字之外——都不解释。
- 「离开老城区，字迹会消失」这一条本章不测试：沈越不得跨出边界做实验，只让「这批书要离开这家店、这家店要离开这条街」与手上那行字同时在场，把这条规则变成威胁而不是设定说明。
- 禁揭：项目无卷纲，没有可对照的禁揭条目——这就是缺口。在卷纲补齐前，本章按「不解释金手指、不解释遗言、不交代替角的完整身份与来意」处理。

## 章末问题

在书被称走、店被腾空之前，沈越能不能弄清这行字是写给谁的——他凭什么认定，自己也在里面？

## 产物（按序）

前置产物——缺一不可，先落地，再写正文：

1. **`design/characters/沈越.md`**（主角卡）。前置性：本章每个「他要什么」都从这里来——他为什么在这家店里、有没有处置权、缺什么、怕什么。卡不在，正文只能把他写成「一个在整理书的人」，这场戏就没有主角，只有一双手。
2. **`design/characters/<角力者>.md`**（候选 A／B／C 由用户定名后再写）。前置性：本章唯一的对抗关系由他的权限与动机定义；动机悬空，冲突就只能靠嗓门。
3. **`design/wiki/遗言.md`**，或在 `design/wiki/world.md` 的「规则与秩序」下增一节。要把「扉页遗言只有沈越能看见、离开老城区消失」写成可执行规则：什么算遗言、看见的条件（碰到／翻到／独处？）、别人看见的是什么、能否重复看、能否给人看、是不是每本都有。前置性：本章是全书唯一一次「规则示范」，示范错了后面每次都要打补丁；连「对方翻同一页只看见空白」这个动作能不能写，都取决于它。
4. **`design/wiki/书店.md`**。店本身：位置属性、门面、书从哪来、租约与期限这类能落字的事实（街巷名与金额由用户定）。前置性：本章的「濒临倒闭」必须落到具体东西上——谁的店、什么账、什么期限，否则沈越查账、找买家、搬书这些动作没有地面。
5. **`design/outline/vol_1.md`** 与 **`design/outline/vol_1/s1.md`**。前置性：本章该兑现什么承诺、什么必须留给后面，只能由它们给；现在上面两节都只能按通行约束兜底。

本章文件：

- `chapters/chapter_ch1_v1.md`
- `state/characters/沈越.md`（他在店里的位置、为留下那本书付出的代价、他手上那本书）
- `state/foreshadowing.md`（那行字、那张扉页、他留下的那个理由；因无卷纲，「预计回收处」标 TBD 并注明待卷纲）
- `state/progress.md`（第 1 章一节，两行）

## 材料缺口清单（需用户回答，3 条）

1. **沈越和这家店是什么关系、他为什么在这儿？**（雇工／店主亲属／替人看店／无处可去暂住）——推荐：按「替亲友看店的临时工」处理，既无权处置书（构成障碍），又必须整天经手整批书（金手指有地方出现）；不设成店主本人，否则他一开始就有权，这场争夺就没了。
2. **这家店为什么快开不下去、还剩多少时间？**——推荐：用「老城区更新＋租金与客流」这条线，不用拆迁征收。可查的现实依据：武昌老城的昙华林—得胜桥—胭脂路一带确有持续的旧书店生态（老张书舍、《泉之旧书》三十六平米五六万册的二手书店、瓜牛循环书店等），而武汉自 2025 年起推开城市更新三年行动、首批 80 个「小而美」更新片区，历史街区修缮后普遍引入新业态（新华网《武汉「三老」焕新记》、人民日报《武汉聚焦城市更新》、武汉市政府门户网站昙华林报道）。用这条线能让「濒临倒闭」有街道级的现实压力，又不会像拆迁期限那样把全书时间表一次锁死。
3. **金手指的最小规则里，本章要不要让「别人翻同一页看不见」当场被验证？**——推荐：要，且要设为「他人看见的是原有的普通题字（如『某某购于某年』）」，而不是干净的空白。这样每次被发现都可以写成具体风险（对方会问「你在看什么」），也省掉了「为什么这本书没有题字」这种反向线索。
response.reasoning:
Good grounding: 武昌老城区 昙华林—得胜桥—胭脂路 一带确有旧书店生态（老张书舍、泉之旧书 36 平米五六万册、瓜牛循环书店二手书）; 武汉 2025 起城市更新三年行动、首批 80 个"小而美"更新片区，历史街区"修缮+业态升级"，租金与商户更替压力。这足以支撑"濒临倒闭"的现实压力源：老城区更新/房租/客流转。

I don't need more. Maybe one quick check on 旧书收购价/废纸价? Not necessary — the brief can be staged with 收废纸按斤称 without a specific price, and I can flag price as fact-to-check for the writing partner... but the instruction says I'm to settle real-world facts I mustn't assert from memory. I could avoid asserting a number. Better: avoid numbers. But the brief may say "按斤称价" without numbers — fine.

Actually maybe worth a quick check for 拆迁/更新 in 武昌老城区 specifically (得胜桥片区 旧改). Not essential. I have enough: 武汉城市更新三年行动 + 历史街区. Good.

Now, the real problem: design docs are extremely thin. No character cards at all — not even 沈越. The brief requires 沈越 must exist as a character front and an opposing person in the room. That person doesn't exist in docs → must be a "需要用户确认的候选" with 2–3 directions and costs.

Also 前置产物 needed before chapter lands:
1. design/characters/沈越.md — protagonist card missing; the brief can't set his age, why he works in the shop (雇工/店主亲戚/接手的儿子), what he can and can't do, what he lacks. Because everything about "what each person wants" rests on him.
2. design/wiki/ 规则页 for 金手指 — the rule "扉页遗言只有沈越能看见；离开老城区字迹消失" is one line; need: what counts as 遗言（作者/前读者手写?）; how many at a time; can he read others' 批注? does the writing appear on 扉页 only; 触发条件（碰/看/翻到扉页）; 是否一直可见; 是否消耗; 能否告诉别人（会不会失效）。特别是本章第一行字必须"只出现一次且清楚"的边界 → 前置 because 第 1 章是全书的规则示范章.
3. design/characters/<角力者>.md — the person in the room.
4. design/wiki/world.md 补页 — 书店本身（店面、租约、书的来源）以及"老城区"边界如何划（因为"离开老城区字迹消失"需要一个可执行的空间定义）。前置因为本章结尾/章末问题可能涉及边界。
5. design/outline/vol_1.md + vol_1/s1.md — 完全没有卷纲和序号大纲；chapter 1 的"依据"只能是用户意图 + core 一句话；无法判断第 1 章该兑现什么承诺、什么必须留到后面。这条其实是最硬的前置。所以我应该在 依据/前情 里把它作为设计问题提出来。

The user asked: 2. 这一章必须有一个在场的人跟沈越角力…… 请把该人物写成"需要用户确认的候选"，给出 2–3 个方向及各自代价。3. 明确列出前置产物。4. 材料缺口清单最多 3 条，每条附推荐。

Format: exactly the shape given (## 依据 / ## 前情 / ## 这场戏 / ## 必须发生 / ## 不能提前兑现 / ## 章末问题 / ## 产物（按序）). But user also asks for additional lists (候选人物方向、前置产物清单、材料缺口清单). The format says 产物（按序） section lists the files. I can fold 前置产物 into 产物（按序） (since that section already is "products in order"), and add the candidate-person directions inside 这场戏 / 必须发生, and 材料缺口清单... The system prompt says output the brief and nothing else, no notes to the user. But the user explicitly demands these lists. User instruction here is a plan-gate request that includes deliverable requirements. I'll comply with the user: include 候选人物 inside 这场戏 (as 待确认候选) and add sections for 前置产物 / 材料缺口. To keep the shape, I'll put 前置产物 as a subsection within 产物（按序）(or as bullets there), and add a final "## 材料缺口清单（需用户回答）". That's a deviation but user-requested. I think best: keep the seven headings in order, and add "## 材料缺口清单" after 产物. The 候选人物 inside 这场戏 with 2–3 directions and costs — write it there.

Now design the scene substantively.

Setting: 武汉老城区（武昌 昙华林—得胜桥 一带 或 汉口老里份），一家濒临倒闭的旧书店。It's 武汉老城区, and real old-book ecosystem is 武昌老城区 得胜桥/昙华林. I can reference "老城区" without naming a street (地名 must be user's call). I'll say 老城区的旧书店（具体街巷名待用户定；现实里同类生态集中在武昌老城的昙华林—得胜桥—胭脂路一带，可作选址依据）。Hmm — that's a bit of note-to-user. But it's a 依据-ish grounding. I could keep it minimal: mention I did not name the street.

Protagonist: 沈越. What does he want? Unknown from docs — only "一个在旧书店整理旧书的人". Reasonable: 整理旧书 to 卖/清库，因为店要关门/房租到期。But that's not in docs → the 角力者 candidate and 沈越's stake both hinge on missing facts. I should write the brief so it works under a stated minimal assumption, and flag them as 需确认. The instruction: "凡是需要用户拍板的地方，不要自己编造人名/地名/事件，直接在返回里标出来." So I mark them.

But the brief must be stageable — "enough for the writing partner to stage the scene without coming back to ask you anything." Tension. Resolution: give a concrete scene design with the uncertain person as 候选 A/B/C, each with what the scene becomes. That's what the user asked. So 这场戏 will present the common core plus the alternatives.

Let me design the scene:

## 前情

沈越在老城区一家快要开不下去的旧书店里整理旧书；这批书没有书目、没有记录，只有堆。书店的命运不掌握在他手里：能决定这些书卖给谁、按什么价卖、什么时候清空的，是另一个人（候选见下），而那个人已经在给这件事收尾。沈越今天要做的只是"分堆"——能卖的、不能卖的、按斤称掉的。这一章开始时，他还不知道自己翻开的那一页会给他一样别人拿不到的东西。（设计问题：本章"必须兑现的承诺"与"不能提前兑现"清单应由卷纲给出，现在只能按第一章的通行约束处理，待卷纲补齐后校订。）

## 这场戏

地点：武汉老城区这家旧书店店内（街巷与店名待用户定；地段属性是"老城区、街面窄、附近有学校或老居民"这一类，选址依据见 材料缺口）；时间：关门前的两三个小时，一天里唯一还能做成生意的时段。

在场：沈越（整理旧书的人，没有处置权，只有干活的责任）；以及必须在场的那个人——他要在这几小时里让这批书有一个去处，他有权，也有他的时间压力。两个人的目标在这一批书上正面冲突：对方要"清空"，沈越要"分清"。

矛盾的具体形态：不是吵架，是同一个动作被两个人往反方向用——沈越每从堆里挑出一本，对方就把它归回"称掉的那一堆"，理由是"来不及了/没人买"。

金手指的落地方式：沈越在一本书的扉页上看见一行手写字。他不是一个人看见的——对方就在店里，所以他的第一反应不能是"这是什么"，只能是"这本书不能走"，而他给不出真理由。

**在场者：需用户拍板的候选（名字与关系留白，不代拟）**
- A. 店主本人（沈越帮他整理、他准备把店关掉或转出去）。代价：要有自己的非"关店"动机才不塌成一个功能性角色，得单独立卡；并且"他看不看得见字迹"必须先由规则页定死，否则第一章就埋下规则漏洞。收益：他和书有几十年的关系，一句"这本书从哪来的"就能把遗言连到店的历史上，后续可复用。
- B. 房东/来收租或谈续租、接手店面的人。代价：现实数字（租金、期限、老城区更新的具体做法）要落到文档里，不能凭记忆写；此人容易变成一次性的敲门人，且一旦定下"限期"，全书时间表就被这条线锁住。收益：压力外部化、时限清楚，沈越的无力感最直接。
- C. 收旧货/收废纸的（按斤称，定期来）。代价：身份低、话语权小，若只来一次就是道具；若设为长期线人，就得先定他和沈越的关系史，等于多一张卡。收益：最能把"那本书"从沈越手里实际拿走——冲突可以落在手上，不落在嘴上；按斤称这个动作本身就把"书的命"压成重量，和遗言形成直接反差。
（推荐 A 在场、C 稍后到场：A 给关系与历史，C 给即时的物理威胁；若只想上一张新角色卡，选 B。）

## 依据

项目没有卷纲、也没有序号大纲（`design/outline/vol_1.md`、`design/outline/vol_1/s1.md` 都不存在），所以本章没有序号大纲里的承诺可供对照，这是需要先补上的前提。按用户意图和 core 的「金手指 / 超常设定」，本章承担全书第一次「规则生效」：变的是信息和立场——沈越在别人正要处置同一批书的当下，第一次拿到一条只有他有的、关于某一本书的信息，因此第一次对一本书的去留有主张，并为这主张付出代价。

## 前情

沈越在武汉老城区一家开不下去的旧书店里整理旧书；这批书没有书目、没有登记，只是堆着。书的处境不由他做主：决定这批书卖给谁、按什么价、什么时候清走的，是另一个人（候选见下），那个人已经在给这件事收尾。沈越今天该做的只是分堆——能卖的、不能卖的、按斤称掉的。开场时他还不知道，自己随手翻开的那一页里，藏着一样别人拿不到的东西。（设计问题：本章该兑现的承诺与禁揭清单应由卷纲给出，现在只能按第一章的通行约束兜底；卷纲补齐后这一节要校订。）

## 这场戏

地点：这家旧书店店内。街巷名、店名都不定，地段属性是「老城区、街面窄、周边有老居民或学校」，选址要不要用下面的现实依据，由用户拍板——我不代拟地名。时间：关门前的两三个小时，也是这家店一天里唯一还可能有进账的时段。

在场：沈越——整理旧书的人，没有处置权，只有干活的责任；加上那个必须在场的人——他要在这几个小时里给这批书找到去处，他有权，也有他自己的时间压力。两人的目标在同一批书上正面冲突：对方要「清空」，沈越要「分清」。冲突的具体形态不是吵架，是同一个动作被两个人往反方向用：沈越每从堆里挑出一本，对方就把它归回「称掉的那一堆」，理由是「来不及了」「没人买」。

金手指出现的地方：沈越在一本书的扉页上看见一行手写字。他不是一个人看见的——对方就在店里，所以他的第一个反应不能是「这是什么」，只能是「这本书不能走」，而他说不出真实理由。这一章的张力全在「他有一个不能说的理由，却要为它当场付钱、当场撒一个谎」。

**在场者：需要用户拍板的候选（名字与关系留白，不代拟）**

- **A. 店主本人**（沈越帮他整理，他正准备把店关掉或转出去）。代价：他得有一个「关店」之外的自己的动机，否则会塌成功能性角色，必须单独立卡；「他看不看得见字迹」必须先由规则页定死，否则第一章就留下规则漏洞。收益：他和这些书有几十年的关系，一句「这本书哪来的」就能把遗言连到店的来路上，后续一直能用。
- **B. 房东，或来收租／谈续租、看店面接手的人**。代价：租金、期限、老城区更新怎么做，这些现实细节都得落进文档，不能凭记忆写；此人容易变成只上门一次的敲门人；更要紧的是一旦定下「限期」，全书时间表就被这条线锁住。收益：压力外部化、时限清楚，沈越的无力感最直接。
- **C. 收旧货／收废纸的**（按斤称，定期来）。代价：身份低、话语权小，只来一次就是道具；若设成长期线人，得先定他和沈越的关系史，等于多写一张角色卡。收益：最能把那本书从沈越手里实际拿走——冲突落在手上而不是嘴上；「按斤称」这个动作本身就把书的命压成重量，与扉页上的遗言形成最直接的反差。

推荐 A 在场、C 稍后到场（A 给关系与来路，C 给即时的物理威胁）；若只想新增一张角色卡，选 B。**选哪一个、这个人叫什么，是用户拍板项。**

## 必须发生

- 对方定下一个截止时间，并当着沈越的面处置这批书（说出去处、安排称重或叫车），要他在同一段时间里把「能卖的」挑完——障碍是整批书没有书目也没有买家，他只能一本一本地翻，翻书的速度本身就是压力。

- 对方把那本书判进「称掉」或「我拿去送人」的那一堆并伸手去拿，沈越用一个对方能接受的理由把它留下——谎言或交易（按价买下、说有人订了），绝不能是「上面有字」。他为此付出当场可见的代价：掏钱、被记一笔、或答应一件他不想答应的事。
- 对方翻同一页，什么也没看见（或只看见原有的题字）；「只有我能看见」因此不是沈越的猜测，而是被别人当场否定的东西——同时他也明白这件事不能说出口。
- 沈越把那本书从「要清掉的」挪到自己那一摞，并做出一个超出本职的动作（追这本书从哪来、记住它原来的主人是谁），随即被自己的处境反驳：他连自己明天还在不在这家店都不知道。
- 对方临走留下一个条件或一个时间点，把「书的处置」和「沈越还能不能待在这儿」绑在一起——本章在此结束，不解决。

## 不能提前兑现

- 那行字是谁写的、写给谁的、为什么是这一本——不查、不解释、不推断；沈越这一章只拿到「有一行字」和「只有他能看见」，不得把它读成任务、名单或密码。
- 金手指的来由、代价、能不能给别人看、能不能扩展到扉页手写字之外——都不解释。
- 「离开老城区，字迹会消失」这一条本章不测试：沈越不得跨出边界做实验，只让「这批书要离开这家店、这家店要离开这条街」与手上那行字同时在场，把这条规则变成威胁而不是设定说明。
- 禁揭：项目无卷纲，没有可对照的禁揭条目——这就是缺口。在卷纲补齐前，本章按「不解释金手指、不解释遗言、不交代替角的完整身份与来意」处理。

## 章末问题

在书被称走、店被腾空之前，沈越能不能弄清这行字是写给谁的——他凭什么认定，自己也在里面？

1. **`design/characters/沈越.md`**（主角卡）。前置性：本章每个「他要什么」都从这里来——他为什么在这家店里、有没有处置权、缺什么、怕什么。卡不在，正文只能把他写成「一个在整理书的人」，这场戏就没有主角，只有一双手。
